title: Popular Defence Forces Act (1989)
text:
(Translated from Arabic)
Popular Defence Forces Act of 1989 (5 November 1989)
Name of Act 1. The present Act is called “The Popular Defence Forces Act
of 1989”.
Abrogation and 2. The Popular Defence Forces Act of 1981 is hereby abrogated,
exception
although all the regulations, orders and rules issued pursuant thereto shall
remain in force unless they are amended or repealed under the terms of the
present Act.
Interpretation 3. In the present Act, unless the context suggests otherwise:1
(a) “The Commander” means the Commander of the Popular
Defence Forces.
“The Commander-in-Chief” means the most senior officer who has
assumed the command of the People’s Armed Forces.
“The Popular Defence Forces” means the forces established
pursuant to article 4.
“The Council” means the Council of the Popular Defence Forces
established pursuant to paragraph 1 of article 9.
(b) Any word or term for which no interpretation is given in the
present Act shall have the interpretation given in the Popular Armed
Forces Act.
Establishment of 4. Paramilitary forces known as the “Popular Defence Forces” shall be
the Popular
established under the authority of the Commander-in-Chief and shall be
Defence Forces
made up of Sudanese citizens who satisfy the criteria laid down in the
present Act.

- 2 -
Aims of the 5. The Popular Defence Forces shall endeavour to train their members
Popular Defence
in civil and military protection and shall raise their security awareness,
Forces
instil in them a military spirit and military traditions and discipline so that
they will be able to assist the People’s Armed Forces and other regular
forces whenever needed.
Functions of the 6. The Popular Defence Forces shall perform the following functions:
Popular Defence
(a) Assist the People’s Armed Forces and other regular forces
Forces
whenever needed;
(b) Contribute to the defence of the nation and help to deal with
crises and public disasters;
(c) Any other task entrusted to them by the Commander-in-
Chief himself or pursuant to a recommendation of the Council.
Appointment of 7. (1) The Commander-in-Chief shall appoint a commander for
the Commander
the Popular Defence Forces from among the officers of the People’s
Armed Forces and other regular forces who shall have at least the rank of
Brigadier General.
(2) The Commander-in-Chief may appoint any number of
officers from the People’s Armed Forces to serve under the Commander.
(3) The Council, with the approval of the
Commander-in-Chief, may select any number of members of other regular
forces to work in the leadership of the Popular Defence Forces and serve
under the Commander.
Duties of the 8. The Commander shall issue:2
Commander
(a) With the approval of the Commander-in-Chief, an annual
training manual;
(b) With the approval of the Commander-in-Chief, the standing
orders of the Popular Defence Forces;
(c) The orders and instructions needed to direct the
performance, maintain the discipline and cohesion and guarantee the
efficiency of the Popular Defence Forces.
2 Ibid.

- 3 -
Establishment 9. (1) A consultative council, known as “The Council of the
and composition
Popular Defence Forces” shall be established and shall be constituted as
of the Council
follows:3
(a) Chief of Staff (Chairman);
(b) Commander of the Popular Defence Forces (Rapporteur);
(c) Director-General of the Police Forces;
(d) Deputy Director of the Department of Military Affairs;
(e) Representative of the Ministry of Education (members);
(f) Representative of the security forces;
(g) Representative of the Office of Federal Government;
(h) Any other individual whom the Commander-in-Chief
deems suitable.
(2) The regulations shall establish where and how Council
meetings shall be run and the procedure for taking decisions and making
recommendations.
Council’s areas 10. (1) The Council shall have competence for advising the
of competence
Commander-in-Chief on all matters affecting the Popular Defence Forces.
(2) Without prejudice to paragraph 1, the Council shall have
competence for providing advice on the following:
(a) The areas in which the Popular Defence Forces should be
established;
(b) Issues relating to military training of the Popular Defence
Forces and national and cultural education for their members;
(c) Issues relating to the duties and activities of the Popular
Defence Forces;
(d) Any other subjects relating to the Popular Defence Forces.
3 Ibid.

- 4 -
Conditions of 11. In order to be accepted as a volunteer in the Popular Defence
acceptance as a
Forces a person must satisfy the following criteria:
volunteer in the
Popular Defence (a) He must have been born Sudanese;
Forces
(b) He must be not less than 16 years old;
(c) He must be medically fit;
(d) He must be of good conduct.
Call-up of the 12. The Commander-in-Chief may issue an order for the call-up of the
Popular Defence
Popular Defence Forces in any of the following circumstances:
Forces
(a) For training;
(b) At times of crises and disasters;
(c) When a war breaks out or is expected to break out;
(d) In any other cases that he thinks appropriate.
Release of 13. The directors of government departments, public institutions and
volunteers
agencies and public and private enterprises, or any other employee, shall
release a person who has been accepted or called up by the Popular
Defence Forces.
Training 14. (1) The Popular Defence Forces shall receive training based on
the annual training manual issued by the Commander-in-Chief pursuant to
article 8.
(2) Without prejudice to paragraph 1, training shall consist of
the following programmes:
(a) Military training;
(b) Civil defence training;
(c) National education;
(d) Cultural education.
Proportion of 15. The proportion of persons recruited to the Popular Defence Forces
recruits
shall not exceed 25 per cent of the total workforce of a single institution,
whether in the public sector or the private sector.

- 5 -
Rights and 16. (1) A person enlisted in the Popular Defence Forces shall retain
privileges
his right to a job, a salary, raises and promotions in the public and private
sectors during the period of training and call-up, provided that the private
sector does not have to pay the salaries of those it employs for a period of
more than three months.
(2) An enlisted person who is a student shall retain the right to
continue his studies after completing his period of service.
(3) For the purposes of the National Service Act, an enlisted
person shall be credited for every period of time he spends in the service
of the Popular Defence Forces.
Applicable law 17. During the period of training and call-up, members of the Popular
Defence Forces shall be subject to military laws and the military courts
shall have competence for trying them.
Exemption from 18. A person enlisted in the Popular Defence Forces shall be exempted
service
from service during the training and call-up periods for any of the
following reasons:
(a) Health;
(b) Discipline;
(c) Family;
(d) Security.
Budget 19. The Popular Defence Forces shall receive a separate budget from
the Ministry of Defence which shall be disbursed according to the
directives of the Commander-in-Chief.
Issuance of 20. (1) The Commander-in-Chief may issue the regulations, orders
regulations
and rules necessary for the implementation of the present Act and regulate
all matters for which the Popular Defence Forces have responsibility,
providing them with training and weapons and ensuring discipline and
cohesion.

- 6 -
(2) Without prejudice to paragraph 1, these regulations, orders
and rules may provide for the following:
(a) The extension of service in the Popular Defence Forces and
progression through the ranks;
(b) Uniforms and training activities;
(c) Monthly pay during the call-up and training period;
(d) Appointments, allowances, subsistence, accommodation
and travel expenses during the training and call-up period;
(e) The procedures for enrolling in the Popular Defence Forces.
